sources.title: Annexe II — Arrêté du 18 avril 2012 relatif aux documents et visas exigés pour l'entrée des étrangers sur le territoire des collectivités de Saint-Barthélemy et de Saint-Martin
sources.officialityEvidence: Légifrance publishes the consolidated French ministerial order. The opened Annex II records that it has been in force since 19 June 2025 and lists the passport-specific exemptions for Saint-Martin.
sources.supportingExcerpt: Liste des pays ... dont les titulaires de passeport sont dispensés de visa.

sources.title: Arrêté du 18 avril 2012 relatif aux documents et visas exigés pour l'entrée des étrangers sur le territoire des collectivités de Saint-Barthélemy et de Saint-Martin
sources.officialityEvidence: The authenticated ministerial order sets the territorial visa framework: its Article 3 exempts only free-movement beneficiaries and Annex II entries, and its Article 6 describes exceptional border visas.

sources.title: Visas pour l'outre-mer
sources.publisher: French Ministry of the Interior, Directorate-General for Foreign Nationals in France
sources.officialityEvidence: The French Interior Ministry's current immigration guidance identifies Saint-Martin as an overseas collectivity governed by a specific territorial short-stay visa rather than the Schengen visa.
sources.supportingExcerpt: Le visa de court séjour est spécifique à l'outre-mer.

policies.title: Named ordinary passports: visa-free short visitor entry
policies.summary: The current Saint-Martin Annex II directly lists these ordinary passports as visa-exempt for an ordinary short visit; all have the normal 90-days-in-180-days ceiling unless the schedule states a narrower rule.
conditions: For a visitor stay not exceeding 90 days in any 180-day period, except where the current Annex II gives a more favourable or narrower passport-specific limit. The listed 15-day Saint Lucia rule is separated below.

For AU, BR, JP, KR, MX, SG and US, the Annex II waiver does not cover a remunerated activity where French law requires a work authorisation and it is not produced. This candidate is limited to the ordinary short-visitor purpose.

For GB, this reflects the ordinary British Citizen passport baseline. The Annex II separately limits certain other British-nationality labels; special passports, residence/long-stay-visa waivers, crew and cruise exceptions, transit, public-order restrictions and final admission are not normalized here.

MF denotes Saint Martin (French part), a French overseas collectivity. This is not a Schengen-visa classification, and the table does not establish any electronic visa or routine visa-on-arrival issuance.

policies.title: Biometric ordinary passports: visa-free short visitor entry
policies.summary: The current Saint-Martin Annex II limits the ordinary-passport waiver for these states to biometric passports.
conditions: Only an ordinary biometric passport qualifies. The current Annex II also excludes Serbian passports issued by the Serbian Coordination Directorate from the Serbian waiver.

The ordinary short-visitor waiver is up to 90 days in any 180-day period. Work, residence, transit, special passports, residence-document waivers, entry prohibitions and final admission remain outside this policy.

policies.title: Taiwan ordinary passports with identity-card number: visa-free short visitor entry
policies.summary: The current Annex II limits Taiwan's ordinary-passport waiver to passports that contain an identity-card number.
conditions: The passport must have been issued by Taiwan and contain an identity-card number. The waiver is for an ordinary visitor stay up to 90 days in any 180-day period.
This does not normalize other Taiwan travel documents, work, residence, transit, special passports, entry prohibitions or final admission.

policies.title: Saint Lucia ordinary passports: limited visa-free short visitor entry
policies.summary: The current Annex II gives Saint Lucia ordinary passports a specific shorter visa-free allowance.
conditions: Visa-free visits are limited to 15 days or less, with no more than 120 cumulative days in a 12-month period; this overrides the general 90-days-in-180-days framing.
Work, residence, transit, special passports, entry prohibitions and final admission remain outside this ordinary-passport visitor policy.

policies.title: Unlisted ordinary passports: advance territorial visa required
policies.summary: For the listed ordinary passports, the current order requires a valid French visa because they are neither free-movement beneficiaries nor ordinary-passport entries in the exhaustive Saint-Martin Annex II waiver list.
conditions: This is the ordinary-passport, short-visitor baseline: the order requires a valid French visa where the Annex II waiver does not apply. The territorial visa is a French visa sticker bearing the collectivity for which it is valid, not an eVisa or standard visa on arrival.

A qualifying current French or fully Schengen-applying-state residence permit or long-stay visa can independently waive the Saint-Martin visa for up to 90 days in 180; that document-conditioned route is deliberately not normalized into these passport rows.

The Annex II has narrow pre-existing-French-visa, old-Vanuatu-passport, cruise, crew, transit, exceptional border-visa and special/diplomatic-passport exceptions. These do not change the unconditioned ordinary short-visitor baseline. A border visa is exceptional, requires unforeseeable imperative entry and may be valid no more than 15 days. Final admission remains for border authorities.
